core_obligations: Choose a covering good for both hypotheses (proof lines 1539-1545): starting from s in H(U), pick a covering U on whose members s lifts to sections s_i of G, and refine it, using cofinality, to a covering with Cech H^1(U, F) = 0.
Form the difference cocycle (proof lines 1546-1552): the sections s_{i_0 i_1} = s_{i_1} - s_{i_0} on the fibre products U_{i_0} x_U U_{i_1} lie in F because the s_i lift the same section s.
Use the vanishing of Cech H^1 (proof lines 1553-1558): the cocycle is a coboundary, so there are t_i in F(U_i) with s_{i_0 i_1} = t_{i_1} - t_{i_0} on the overlaps.
Glue (proof lines 1559-1561): the corrected sections s_i - t_i satisfy the sheaf condition and therefore glue to a section of G over U mapping to s, which proves surjectivity.
proof_roadmap: Take s in H(U) and refine a covering on which s lifts to a covering with vanishing Cech H^1.
The lifts differ on overlaps by a Cech 1-cocycle with values in F.
That cocycle is a coboundary by hypothesis, giving correction sections t_i in F.
Then s_i - t_i glue, exhibiting a preimage of s.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for surjectivity of the map G(U) -> H(U) on sections of a short exact sequence of sheaves on a site (statement lines 1523-1536). The content is the combination of two coverings into one: the author must first take a covering on which the section lifts and then refine it, using cofinality, so that Cech H^1 of F vanishes (proof lines 1539-1545). The lifting defect on overlaps is then a Cech 1-cocycle with values in F (proof lines 1546-1552), whose triviality produces correction sections t_i in F(U_i) that make the corrected sections s_i - t_i glue (proof lines 1553-1561). The non-formal point is the cocycle computation and the gluing of the corrected sections. The claim is H2: one standard Cech-cocycle argument, written out in full.
